title: Release hotseat runbook scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal hotseat checklist for release day cutover. Not official runbook — my oriented notes, TODOs, and shortcuts. Use for running the shift and handoff. Keep handy, update as I test.

High-level goals
- Cutover code & infra for release X.Y.Z (rolling canary -> 100% traffic).
- Migrate feature flags for model-routing change.
- Ensure latency SLOs preserved and no regression on embedding/streaming endpoints.
- Validate rollback path and emergency fallback (old model binary + routing). 

Primary contacts (fast dials)
- Oncall SRE: Ben Cho (pager: ben-pager, slack: @bencho)
- RelEng lead: Maya Singh (x1234, slack: @mayasingh)
- Product PM: Omar Ruiz (slack: @omar)
- DB owner (migrations): Priya N. (slack: @priya-db)

Pre-window checklist (T-6h -> T-1h)
- [ ] Confirm canary config PR merged: PR #4921 (serving-runtime). (link above)
- [ ] Verify infra plan: autoscaler policy change for dedicated pools is staged (infra ticket REDW-2145).
- [ ] Export current production routing rules (k8s configmap + git hash). command: kubectl -n redwood get configmap route-policy -o yaml > /tmp/route-policy.before.yaml
- [ ] Snapshot KV cache metrics and sizes (memcached/redis): capture keys count, hit ratio.
- [ ] Take thin DB snapshot (read-replica catchup) and ensure backups are green.
- [ ] Notify channels: #releng, #prod-alerts, #customer-ops. Use template below.
- [ ] Confirm scheduled maintenance windows on pagerduty calendar.

Quick comms template (post-canary success)
- Slack: "Cutover X.Y.Z canary at T+30m: initial canary healthy (p50/p95 within baseline). Rolling to 50% now. Will update at +60m for 100%. If regressions, revert to previous routing version: configmap route-policy@<git-sha>."
- Email to stakeholders: short summary + link to dashboard + rollback ETA.

Cutover steps (hour zero)
1) Toggle canary route to new model variant: 
   - kubectl -n redwood apply -f canary-route.yaml
   - expected: 5-10% traffic diverted, watch traces.
2) Warmup new workers: run small synthetic traffic mix for endpoints (generator script: tools/synth/warmup.sh --mix=chat,embed)
   - check: KV cache warm-up hits increase, new pods have cpu < 60% after warmup
3) Metrics to watch (dashboard): token processing rate, request latency per-route, error rate (5xx), model queue time, GPU util.
4) After 30m stable -> scale canary to 50%: update route weight and autoscaler target.
5) After 60m stable -> 100% and retire old variant.

Backports / PRs to watch (personal list)
- serving-runtime: PR #4921 (canary routing) — merged but double-check changelog
- console: PR #4470 (canary UI toggle) — needs dogfood QA pre-cutover
- dedicated-scaler: branch hotfix/scale-ops-2026 (ensure policy applied)

Verification checklist (post-100%)
- [ ] p50/p95 within 5% of baseline for chat endpoints
- [ ] Embedding vector similarity regression test: run eval harness (scripts/eval/emb-regress.sh) -> compare with baseline artifact id
- [ ] Run smoke: sample of 200 requests across regions; no errors > 0.5%
- [ ] Traces: validate no tail latency spikes (>1s on streaming start)
- [ ] Cost signal: token/sec CPU and GPU efficiency roughly equal or improved (expectation file: optimize/expected-cost-chart.png)

Quick rollback (if needed)
- Criteria: error rate > 1% sustained 5m OR p95 latency > 2x baseline OR severe mem leak in new pods.
- Steps:
  1) Flip route-policy configmap back to previous git sha: kubectl apply -f /tmp/route-policy.before.yaml
  2) Scale old replica set up if scaled down: kubectl -n redwood scale rs serving-old --replicas=3
  3) Disable autoscaler modifications that target new variant
  4) Notify #prod-alerts and product owners
  5) Open bug/incident ticket and tag oncall.

Postmortem / short notes to write if rollback
- Time of decision, trigger metric, command used to revert, pods affected, root cause hypothesis, recovery ETA.

Known gotchas / my notes
- Migration job for KV schema: runs async. If it runs during canary it causes short client 429s. Best to block migrations T-2h -> T+2h.
- Canary UI toggle sometimes lags due to browser caching; prefer CLI kubectl edit to set weight.
- If embedding latency regresses but chat is fine, likely quantization profile mismatch — revert quant config in model registry.
- Watch for increased cold starts in low-traffic regions; keep warmers running for 90m after 100% to stabilize caches.

Commands I use often (copy-paste)
- Save current route: kubectl -n redwood get configmap route-policy -o yaml > /tmp/route-policy.before.yaml
- Apply canary weight: kubectl -n redwood patch configmap route-policy --patch '{"data":{"weight":"10"}}'
- Warmup: scripts/warmup.sh --model=canary --qps=20 --duration=900
- Quick pod logs: k -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime -c runner --tail=200

Notes to self (todo)
- Add stable link to observability dashboard inside PR description before merge.
- Confirm dedicated autoscaler limits with infra (Ilya) — risk: can blow budget on spike.
- Create a short checklist in repo: contrib/release-hotseat.md and link to this doc.

Handoff marker (post-shift)
- When handing to next hotseat: leave 1-line status + last successful canary timestamp + any mitigations active (warmers/feature-flags). E.g. "Handoff: 2026-03-11 14:20 UTC — 100% new model, warmers still active, no regressions observed, watch embeddings for 2h."

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we want an automated rollback window for the embedding pipeline only? (ask product)
- Why did PR#4412 cause a 1.5x p95 bump last test? link to perf trace and root cause analysis.

Random scratch (ideas)
- Small script to snapshot all relevant configmaps + podlists and upload to S3 with timestamp for quick restore.
- Pre-cutover dry-run on staging that mirrors traffic mix for 1h to validate routing and warmup.

End — update this doc after next dry-run and before final ops-runbook merge.
